glyph_origin: Jiajie (假借 phonetic loan) of 鳳 (“fenghuang”) borrowed for sound to represent 風 (“wind”), sometimes with 凡 added as a phonetic. In Warring States Chu manuscripts the character is written as 凡 above 口 (or confused with 同) with one or two phoenix feathers beneath, or as 凡 above a single phoenix feather. In the Qin script the feather was corrupted into 虫, giving the character its modern structure of 凡 above 虫. Shuowen misinterpreted the character 風 by associating it with insects. (Li, 2012)
